Select a 3D rendering backend

Source: R/coord-3d.R
backend_3d.Rd

Select a 3D rendering backend

Usage

backend_3d(
  type = "vector",
  dpi = 144,
  antialias = 2L,
  blend = "linear",
  samples = 64L,
  bounces = 8L,
  seed = 1L,
  aperture = 0,
  focus = NULL,
  light_radius = 5,
  progressive = FALSE,
  batch_size = 8L,
  geometry = "e3",
  observer = c(0, 0, 0),
  facing = diag(3),
  fov = 70,
  max_distance = 10,
  tolerance = 1e-05,
  max_steps = 2048L,
  quotient = NULL,
  light_size = 0.1,
  rasterise = "marked",
  noise_threshold = 0,
  min_samples = 16L,
  denoise = FALSE,
  exposure = 0,
  tone = "clip"
)

Arguments

type

Backend: "vector", "raster", "hybrid", "pathtrace", "raymarch" (an intrinsic view in a Thurston geometry) or "plotter". The plotter backend is the vector backend drawing strokes only: faces and analytic primitives still hide the strokes behind them but are not painted, and consecutive visible pieces of one stroke are drawn as one path, so an SVG device (ggplot2::ggsave(device = "svg")) writes a drawing for a pen plotter. Feature lines (outline_3d()) and model-space hatching (hatch_3d()) make line-only figures of surfaces. Stroke centrelines are clipped to visible intervals, joined within each source polyline, and ordered within each layer and colour by the nearest endpoint, reversing paths to shorten pen travel (as in vpype's linesort). Consecutive points within 0.01 mm or one tenth of a device pixel are combined. Text and labels are drawn last. A hybrid panel rasterises the layers created with raster = TRUE (an argument of every geom_*_3d() layer and of layer_3d()) into one image at dpi and draws the other layers, axes, panes and text as vector graphics. Vector geometry behind the image's opaque coverage is clipped at its pixels, so lines on or behind a rasterised surface stay exact where they are seen.

dpi

Physical raster resolution.

antialias

Positive integer supersampling factor.

blend

Colour space in which the raster backend composites translucent paint and averages antialiasing samples: "linear" light, encoded to sRGB after averaging, or "srgb", which matches the compositing of vector graphics devices.

samples

Maximum path-tracing samples per pixel added by each render.

bounces

Maximum surface or medium scattering interactions per path.

seed

Nonnegative integer seed for pixel and sample indexed randomness.

aperture

Thin-lens radius in aspect-scaled model units; zero is a pinhole.

focus

Focal-plane distance along the camera forward axis, in model units. NULL focuses on the camera target.

light_radius

Angular radius of each directional or head light in degrees.

progressive

Accumulate samples across redraws of the same scene. Changes to geometry, camera, lighting or image dimensions reset accumulation.

batch_size

Samples per native batch; accumulation is independent of batch size and worker count. R can interrupt between batches.

geometry

Intrinsic geometry for the raymarch backend; see geodesic_3d().

observer

Observer coordinates in that geometry's chart.

facing

Orthonormal 3 by 3 matrix whose columns are the camera's right, up and forward tangent vectors in the observer's orthonormal frame.

fov

Vertical intrinsic field of view in degrees.

max_distance

Maximum intrinsic ray arc length.

tolerance

Surface residual and quotient-boundary tolerance.

max_steps

Maximum steps per intrinsic ray.

quotient

List of paired thurston_portal_3d() domain faces.

light_size

Positive point-light softening radius for intrinsic views.

rasterise

Layers a hybrid panel draws into its image: "marked", the layers created with raster = TRUE; "surfaces", which adds every depth-tested layer that draws faces or analytic quadrics; or "all", which adds every depth-tested layer with faces, paths or points. Text stays vector graphics, placed by the image's visibility.

noise_threshold

Nonnegative relative standard-error target. Zero disables adaptive sampling; positive values stop converged pixels after min_samples. Coverage is tested with absolute standard error. Dark channels use a linear-radiance floor of 0.001. Adaptive stopping is an estimate and can introduce stopping bias.

min_samples

Positive minimum sample count before adaptive stopping. At least two samples per independent half buffer are required.

denoise

Apply native nonlinearly weighted first-order regression using independent colour, albedo, normal and depth half buffers.

exposure

Exposure adjustment in stops, applied in linear light.

tone

"clip", "aces" (Narkowicz fit), or "agx" (the Rec.2020 AgX transform with a polynomial contrast approximation).

Value

A ggplot3d_backend configuration for coord_3d() and animate_3d(), validated at construction and use.

Details

The raster backend renders 16-pixel tiles in parallel. The number of worker threads is the option ggplot3d.threads; the default 0 uses one thread per hardware thread, at most two when _R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_ is set. The image does not depend on the thread count.

The native path tracer uses material_3d() BSDFs, a bounding-volume hierarchy, Owen-scrambled Sobol samples, next-event light sampling with power-heuristic multiple importance sampling and Russian roulette. Ambient light is a uniform environment; directional lights are sampled distant disks. Point, head, hemisphere, image environments and emissive triangles contribute. Directional and point intensities retain the Lambert convention of the other backends (incident irradiance is pi times intensity). Absorption volumes use delta tracking for scattering and ratio tracking for shadow transmittance, with conservative per-cell extinction majorants. Isovolumes intersect the trilinear field as a surface. MIP is unavailable. Points and paths use the solid conversion of export_3d(), and SDF layers use the shared sphere tracer. Furniture and text remain vector graphics.

The raymarch backend traces geodesics from an observer inside the geometry. Use annotation_thurston_3d() for balls, cylinders and half-spaces, or traced SDF layers for chart-defined CSG. It draws a full-panel perspective image; Euclidean plot axes and exterior-camera settings have no intrinsic meaning. Lighting is an isotropic point light at the observer, with the ambient and diffuse strengths from light_3d(). Irradiance divides by the area density of geodesic spheres plus light_size^2. Each visible geodesic supplies its own light path, including paths through quotient faces. Intrinsic surfaces are opaque. See geodesic_3d() for charts and numerical accuracy details.

References

Pharr, Jakob and Humphreys (2023). Physically Based Rendering, fourth edition. https://pbr-book.org/4ed/Light_Transport_I_Surface_Reflection/Path_Tracing

Veach (1997). Robust Monte Carlo methods for light transport simulation. Chapter 9. https://graphics.stanford.edu/papers/veach_thesis/ Veach and Guibas (1995). Optimally combining sampling techniques for Monte Carlo rendering. doi:10.1145/218380.218498

Burley (2020). Practical hash-based Owen scrambling. JCGT 9(4). https://jcgt.org/published/0009/04/01/

Bitterli et al. (2016). Nonlinearly weighted first-order regression for denoising Monte Carlo renderings. doi:10.1111/cgf.12954

Novak et al. (2014). Residual ratio tracking for estimating attenuation in participating media. doi:10.1145/2661229.2661292

Narkowicz (2016). ACES filmic tone mapping curve. https://knarkowicz.wordpress.com/2016/01/06/aces-filmic-tone-mapping-curve/

Three.js AgX tone-mapping implementation, adapted from Filament. https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/dev/src/renderers/shaders/ShaderChunk/tonemapping_pars_fragment.glsl.js

Examples

backend_3d("vector")
backend_3d("raster", dpi = 144, antialias = 2)
backend_3d("raster", blend = "srgb")
backend_3d("pathtrace", samples = 8, seed = 1)
backend_3d("pathtrace", samples = 16, noise_threshold = 0.05, denoise = TRUE, tone = "agx")
# \donttest{
d <- expand.grid(x = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 40), y = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 40))
d$z <- sin(pi * d$x) * cos(pi * d$y)
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_surface_3d(fill = "grey80", colour = NA, raster = TRUE) +
  geom_contour_3d(colour = "black") +
  coord_3d(backend = backend_3d("hybrid", dpi = 150))
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_surface_3d(fill = "grey80", colour = NA) +
  coord_3d(backend = backend_3d("hybrid", dpi = 150, rasterise = "surfaces"))
# }
